candidate.answerReason: Tangency determines the dough radius as 3 inches. Subtracting the seven unit-cookie areas leaves 2π square inches, so the positive scrap-cookie radius is √2, agreeing with A.

methods.label: Find the dough radius and preserve area
methods.explanation:
The cookie centers reveal the dough's radius. Let \(O\) be the center of the middle cookie. Each surrounding cookie is tangent to it, so each surrounding center is \(1+1=2\) inches from \(O\).

Let \(T\) be the dough's center and \(R>1\) its radius. Each surrounding cookie is internally tangent to the dough boundary, so its center is \(R-1\) inches from \(T\). Thus the six distinct surrounding centers lie on both a circle of radius \(2\) centered at \(O\) and a circle of radius \(R-1\) centered at \(T\). Two distinct circles have at most two common points, so these circles coincide. Consequently \(R-1=2\), giving \(R=3\).

The seven cookies have disjoint interiors, so the leftover area is
\[
\pi(3)^2-7\pi(1)^2=2\pi.
\]
Reshaping preserves the amount of dough. Because the thickness stays the same, it also preserves area. If \(r>0\) is the scrap cookie's radius, then
\[
\pi r^2=2\pi,
\qquad r^2=2.
\]
The radius must be positive, so \(r=\boxed{\sqrt2}\) inches, choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
